open_points.subject: answer_request notification and response handling
open_points.text: answer_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST check one request in exactly this order, the first failure deciding: the byte length of request_bytes is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant, else invalid_request; authenticate_token with presented_token gives an Actor, else unauthorized with one fixed reason that reveals nothing about any record; for tools/call, the message names a catalogue operation and fits that operation's request model with no unknown field — a field typed X | None fitting when it is absent or JSON null — and every bound below, else invalid_request; the actor may call that operation by the actor table, else not_permitted; only then is the operation's handler called (A16 rule 1). initialize, ping and tools/list name no catalogue operation and are answered after the size and token checks, as the note on methods says.
open_points.other_text: answer_request: [BEHAVIOR] The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks. A JSON object whose jsonrpc is "2.0" with a string method and an id is a request; one with a method and no id is a notification and one with no method a response: both are answered with empty bytes and change nothing. A request's method decides: initialize answers the result {protocolVersion: the imported MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION constant, capabilities: {tools: {listChanged: false}}, serverInfo: {name: the imported MCP_SERVER_NAME constant, version: the imported MCP_SERVER_VERSION constant}} whatever version its params ask, and keeps no state; ping answers an empty result object; tools/list answers {tools: [...]} as below, ignoring any cursor; tools/call names the catalogue operation in params.name and carries its request in params.arguments, which then pass the remaining checks of the first note.
open_points.question: Must an oversized or unauthenticated notification/response produce the first-failure refusal required before parsing, or must every notification/response return empty bytes?

open_points.subject: answer_request handling of internal_error exceptions
open_points.text: answer_request: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST call the handler of the named operation, whose name is handle_ followed by the operation name — exactly one of handle_accept_binding, handle_activate_flow_version, handle_add_trial_case, handle_cancel_run, handle_capture_failed_execution, handle_compose_flow_version, handle_decide_effect_approval, handle_get_binding, handle_get_contract_version, handle_get_flow, handle_get_flow_version, handle_get_implementation, handle_get_repair_view, handle_get_run, handle_get_slot, handle_grant_standing_approval, handle_issue_contract_version, handle_list_records, handle_propose_binding, handle_prove_flow_version, handle_read_fixture_file, handle_read_spooled_file, handle_release_run, handle_resolve_unknown_outcome, handle_resume_run, handle_revoke_standing_approval, handle_roll_back_slot, handle_start_run, handle_submit_implementation and handle_try_implementation — with the Actor and the validated request, encode its answer as the tool result — values as JSON text, file bytes as base64 — and turn any exception the handler raises into a refusal answer through translate_failure, except any failure translate_failure answers internal_error — StopRequiredError, StoreInternalError or any unexpected exception, whatever the handler — which it lets propagate to serve_kernel unchanged, since a store change may already be written and only the next start derives every run again.
open_points.other_text: answer_request: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns the bytes of one JSON-RPC 2.0 response as UTF-8 JSON, or empty bytes for a notification or a response. A tools/call that reached its operation returns the result {content: [{type: "text", text: T}], isError: B}: T is the answer of the operation as JSON text and B false, or T is the RefusalAnswer as the JSON object {code, reason} and B true for every refusal decided once the operation is known — fit, bounds, canonical form, permission, or translate_failure of an exception the handler raised; every refusal code is a member of = models.RefusalCode.
open_points.question: Must a handler exception translated as internal_error propagate unchanged to serve_kernel, or must it be returned by answer_request as an isError tool result like every translated handler exception?
